title: Principal Directions, Random Coverage and Data Mixtures
subtitle: DRAM · ProMix · Human-feedback summarization
intro: Main reads examine DRAM’s subspace coverage and ProMix’s reference-model correction. Briefs cover rotational scheduling, inference compute and substantive extensions of earlier papers. The classic revisits human-feedback summarization, separating reward gains from human-preference gains.
window: November 21–24, 2026 (America/New_York; emphasis on updates since the previous issue, with a 72-hour overlap)

articles.paper: DRAM: Memory-Efficient Muon via Rank Reallocation in Principal-Random Subspaces
articles.authors: Bai, Haomin · Yu, Dingzhi · Zhao, Xuling · Yang, Sifan · Wang, Yibo · Zhang, Lijun
articles.title: DRAM: low rank should not retain only the strongest directions

blocks.text: For X∈R^(m×n), take m≤n. Each DRAM block keeps the leading r left singular vectors R of a stochastic gradient and draws q uniform complementary directions P, with total rank k=r+q. Increasing the random share later addresses true-gradient directions missed when noise dominates TopSVD. [1]

blocks.label: The paper’s coverage lemma retains the principal subspace and covers its complement in expectation with strength δ; q>0 supplies this guarantee.

blocks.tex: \widehat G_t=B^\top G_t,\quad H_t=(1-\beta)H_{t-1}+\beta\widehat G_t,\qquad X_{t+1}=X_t-\eta B\operatorname{polar}(H_t)
blocks.label: The paper’s within-block update; reset H=βĜ at block starts. Here β weights the gradient, unlike the common momentum-coefficient convention.

blocks.text: Persistent state falls from O(mn) to O((m+n)k), with spectral normalization on k×n momentum. C4 training uses 1.2B/2.5B/7B tokens for 60M/130M/350M models. The table reports mean accuracy over seven zero-shot tasks, not training loss. [1]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Rates concern the average nuclear norm of gradients, exact polar maps, unbiased finite-variance gradients and operator/nuclear smoothness, with nondecreasing coverage factors. They do not establish an end-to-end guarantee for finite NS. Best low-memory performance does not mean matching full-state Muon. [1]

articles.paper: ProMix: Efficient Data Mixture Optimization for Robotic Imitation via Proxy-Reference DRO
articles.authors: Sima, Qie · Xue, Wei · Guo, Yike
articles.title: ProMix: separate irreducible difficulty from learning headroom

blocks.text: Following the proxy/reference approach of DoReMi (2023) and robotic Re-Mix (2024), ProMix learns domain weights with small models. Lᵢ is mean behavioral-cloning loss on domain i; a frozen reference θR provides a baseline while proxy θP and domain distribution p are alternately optimized. [2]

blocks.label: The paper’s objective: high absolute loss may reflect noise; positive entropy in the maximization discourages weight collapse. The reference is not known Bayes risk.
The paper’s exponentiated-gradient update. Proxy search samples 128 examples from every domain each step, then weights by p; this is not an equal-cost step sampling a single domain from p.

blocks.text: Reference and proxy each train for 100k steps. The 15M count covers trainable parameters, excluding frozen encoders. Weight search totals 11 GPU-hours; weights transfer to 50M and 7B VLAs without retuning. The paper reports 9,500 real-robot evaluations on Open-X: average success rises from 68.4% to 76.2%, and worst-domain success from 51.4% to 68.5%. [2]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The 11-versus-192 GPU-hour comparison concerns mixture search at 7B, not a 17× speedup of all VLA training. Transfer of small-model domain rankings is empirical in the tested tasks, not a general guarantee. [2]

articles.paper: From Learning Rates to Rotational Schedules: Finite-Horizon Theory on the Sphere
articles.authors: Graldi, Jacopo · Orvieto, Antonio · Koloskova, Anastasia
articles.title: Rotational schedules depend on parameter scale
articles.evidence: Read introduction and relevant Section 2 text

blocks.text: For scale-invariant GD, the rotational coefficient is η/‖x‖². The text optimizes a last-iterate bound on a geodesically convex spherical cap, with an asymptotically linear-decay profile. Norm dynamics change the rotation induced by the same LR in ordinary Adam/Muon. This is not global nonconvex LLM convergence theory. [3]

articles.paper: Stein Guidance without Gradients: Discretization Uniform Diffusion Inference Time Scaling beyond Particle SMC
articles.authors: Zhu, Youheng · Wang, Chenyang · Chen, Minshuo · Lu, Yiping
articles.title: Stein Guidance: whole-path correction

blocks.text: Derivative-free candidate selection is paired with whole-path independence MH correction. The abstract claims finite-grid TV bounds with step-count-uniform constants under uniform value/spatial regularity; arbitrary learned values need not satisfy these conditions. [4]

articles.title: TTC4TS: frozen forecasting with candidate synthesis

blocks.text: Candidates from augmentation, retrieval or adapters are ranked or aggregated around a frozen time-series backbone, studying gains with candidate count. A frozen backbone does not imply all generators and synthesizers are training-free. [5]

articles.title: TT-RSI: contextual recursion and weight distillation

blocks.text: The method re-solves with the previous complete solution as reference, then distills successive refinements. The abstract compares matched test-time-scaling budgets. Its limiting analysis does not imply unlimited self-improvement for arbitrary unlabeled models. [6]

articles.paper: Unlocking the Power of Loops in Pretrained LLMs with Loop Residuals
articles.authors: Zhao, Xuanlei · Xu, Hailun · Wang, Kai · Luo, Yang · Ren, Yingxuan · Zhu, Zirui · Lou, Yuxuan · Xu, Kun · Wang, Yan · Sarkar, Kanchan · You, Yang
articles.title: LoopRes: distinguish loop outputs and build incrementally

blocks.text: Looped layers attend to earlier loop outputs with learned loop-identity keys and a bounded residual window. This studies adding scalable computation to existing LLMs; the abstract’s 2× compute is a budget comparison, not an equal-cost gain. [7]

articles.paper: When Wrong Answers Remain Unsettled: Failure Dynamics in Recurrent Reasoners
articles.authors: Zang, Jiucheng · Peng, Congkai · Wei, Yankai
articles.title: Wrong endpoints need not be stable attractors

blocks.text: Extending HRM recurrence without noise changes many wrong answers; matched-compute depth extension outperforms the tested frozen noise. Finite-horizon evidence from one main checkpoint does not exclude asymptotic attractors. [8]

articles.paper: Self-Refining VLA Sampling
articles.authors: Duan, Jeff · Sharma, Arjun · Cruden, Jennifer · Tibrewal, Vansh
articles.title: Self-refinement of VLA action samples

blocks.text: Predict-and-Perturb refinement is adapted to flow-generated action trajectories as an alternative inference-compute route to large candidate pools or external correctors. Abstract only; no guarantee across arbitrary robots or budgets is asserted. [9]

articles.authors: Zhong, Yishan · Li, Jieru · Ding, Xuanzhe · Wang, Shaunna · Yang, Yanxin · Nnamdi, Micky C. · Tamo, J. Ben · Wang, Yifei · Yuan, Yining · Marteau, Benoit L. · Tan, Shaun Q. Y. · Moore, Carrie · Xie, Luyu · Xie, Yang · Shi, Wenqi · Wang, May D.
articles.title: MedCoast: budgeted search over semantic prefixes

blocks.text: Offline clustering of same-prefix reasoning steps trains a lightweight PRM, which prioritizes online expansions. The abstract compares fixed-budget self-consistency. Full experiments were not read; the largest task gain is not an average gain. [10]

articles.paper: Fuzzy e-Means: Fuzzy c-Means on Large Data with Moving-Average Mini-Batch Updates
articles.authors: Tiwari, Paritosh · Rathore, Punit
articles.title: Fuzzy e-Means: transferring batch/step scaling rules

blocks.text: Moving averages and batch/step rules transfer from e-means to fuzzy clustering, with hard-assignment initialization and relocation disabled. Small low-dimensional problems can remain slower; no universal speedup is claimed. [11]

articles.title: WeMM-Ecom: staged increases in domain-data proportion

blocks.text: The report describes two-stage continued pretraining with increasing e-commerce mixture proportions, followed by hybrid-thinking post-training. Included for its substantive data-mixing recipe; abstract only, without inferring precise scaling exponents from model rankings. [12]

articles.paper: How to build and maintain an agentic evaluation
articles.authors: Avijit Ghosh · Ben Burtenshaw · Irene Solaiman
articles.title: Verifier audits: pass rates are not reliable completion

blocks.text: On eight synthetic-spectrum development tasks, checking only a peak-height ratio admits a shortcut that never fits the spectrum; fit checks are needed. Three-rollout pass@3 is 7/8, while success in all three runs, pass^3, is 1/8. These answer different reliability questions. The small development set does not establish deployment generalization. [27]

classic.title: Why reward-model scores are not human preferences
classic.paper: Learning to summarize from human feedback
classic.authors: Nisan Stiennon · Long Ouyang · Jeff Wu · Daniel M. Ziegler · Ryan Lowe · Chelsea Voss · Alec Radford · Dario Amodei · Paul Christiano
classic.dateNote: NeurIPS 2020; first posted September 2, 2020; read v3: February 15, 2022

recognition.label: 3,702 citations in the queried OpenAlex record (November 24, 2026)

classic.question: At a matched KL budget, how would an independent labeling budget distinguish reward-model error, preference-distribution shift and insufficient policy optimization?

blocks.text: After preference learning by Christiano et al. (2017) and language-model fine-tuning by Ziegler et al. (2019), this NeurIPS 2020 work joins comparison labeling, reward learning and PPO for summarization. Let x be a post and y a summary of at most 48 tokens. The target is labeler preference rather than ROUGE itself. [28]

blocks.tex: P_\theta(y_w\succ y_l\mid x)=\sigma(r_\theta(x,y_w)-r_\theta(x,y_l)),\quad\mathcal L_{\rm RM}=-\mathbb E\log P_\theta(y_w\succ y_l\mid x)
blocks.label: The paper’s preference model: pairwise comparisons identify score differences, not calibrated absolute summary quality.

blocks.tex: R(x,y)=r_\theta(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\rm SFT}(y\mid x)},\quad J(\pi)=\mathbb E_x\!\left[\mathbb E_\pi r_\theta-\beta D_{\rm KL}(\pi\|\pi_{\rm SFT})\right]
blocks.label: The paper’s sampled reward and its expectation; KL references SFT, not the changing old policy. PPO updates the policy.

blocks.tex: \pi^*(y\mid x)=\frac{\pi_{\rm SFT}(y\mid x)e^{r_\theta(x,y)/\beta}}{Z(x)},\qquad J_x(\pi)=\beta\log Z(x)-\beta D_{\rm KL}(\pi\|\pi^*)
blocks.label: Explanatory derivation for each x: with fixed reward, β>0, finite Z and compatible support, completing the KL yields the ideal optimum. This is not a paper theorem that finite PPO training attains it.
My error decomposition: u denotes ideal preference utility and e modeling error. Reducing β amplifies both; KL regularization does not automatically eliminate reward hacking.

blocks.text: The paper releases 64,832 TL;DR comparisons. PPO’s value network is separate from the policy and initialized from the reward model; all three have the same size in the described experiments. Section 4.3 varies optimization strength against an earlier reward model and finds eventual deterioration in human preference despite rising predicted preference. [28]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Read the method and overoptimization experiments; not reproduced. Preferences depend on instructions, labelers and summary distributions. Reward-validation accuracy and true utility after optimization are different metrics. [28]
